Figure 1:High-Quality Videos Generated by RepForcing.The examples span human activities, animal behavior, and stylized scenes,
showing details such as clothing folds, fur, and vegetation. Across the
displayed frames, subjects change pose and position while retaining their
appearance and surrounding scene structure.

Figure 2:RepForcing Initialization Better Preserves Generation Quality as Sampling Steps Decrease.Rows compare three initialization strategies: teacher-forced AR training
followed by ODE distillation, teacher-forced AR training followed by consistency
distillation, and direct representation-space initialization, from top to
bottom. All results are shown before subsequent refinement. Columns show 4, 8, and 12 sampling steps from
left to right, with two frames per setting for the same prompt.
With more denoising steps, ODE initialization approaches the visual quality
of RepForcing. At four steps, however, the intermediate-teacher initializations
exhibit blur or structural artifacts, while RepForcing maintains coherent
subject and scene structure.

Figure 3:Representation Forcing Initialization Pipeline.Training videos are encoded into clean latent blocks by a VAE encoder.
The trainable causal DiT reconstructs clean blocks from noisy inputs,
conditioned on preceding clean blocks under teacher forcing.
The predicted and target video latents are passed separately through the same
truncated, frozen Wan2.1-14B to obtain features𝐟^\hat{\mathbf{f}}and𝐟\mathbf{f}. A token-wise cosine loss compares these features, with
stop-gradient (sg\operatorname{sg}) on the target branch. Gradients propagate
through the frozen extractor to update the causal DiT. This initialization
replaces intermediate AR teacher training and causal ODE distillation.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of chunk-wise distilled autoregressive
models.For each of four prompts, three sampled frames are shown for CausVid,
Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, Causal-rCM, and RepForcing. The RepForcing examples
retain visible fur strands and facial detail in the character scene, together
with clothing folds, hanging blossoms, and rock textures in the human scenes.
Changes in body and hand pose are visible across the sampled frames.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison of frame-wise autoregressive models.Each quadrant shows three sampled frames for the same prompt across Causal
Forcing, Causal Forcing++, and RepForcing (top to bottom). The examples depict
a girl peeling an orange (top left), a mountaineer overlooking a frozen fjord
(top right), a mother bird feeding her chicks (bottom left), and a woman
holding flowers above a lake (bottom right).
